after:
Every crank revolution turns the top roller one third of a turn, so the cane advances one third of the roller's circumference. The crown gears have equal tooth counts. The top roller turns one way and both bottom rollers turn the other way, so at each nip the two facing surfaces move together at the same speed and pull the stalk through without slipping. Juice is credited as each part of the stalk passes a nip. After one crank revolution, 96% of the stalk has passed the feed nip and been crushed once. Its tail is still on the chute, 0.22 units short of the nip. The status line follows the oldest stalk from chute to feed nip, then over the turnplate, then through the second squeeze and out as bagasse.

The front housing is an open frame of posts, bars and bearing bosses, so the chute and the feed nip can be seen. Between the nips the ribbon is hidden behind the roller ends, just as it would be on a real mill. Press **Inspection: remove front cheek** to see it. This optional section removes the front housing and cuts the rollers, journals, turnplate and chute on the plane of the cane lane. The orange faces are the cut surfaces, with the ribbon lying between the roller sections.

*Idealizations:* there is no steam pressure, torque, friction or real extraction model. The juice values are fixed teaching shares per stalk, and a second stalk can't be fed while the chute is still occupied.
title: Steam-driven sugar-cane mill · new generation
before:
An *engenho* crushes sugar cane between heavy rollers to release its juice. In this steam-powered version, a **slider-crank** turns the piston's back-and-forth motion into rotation. A **3:1 gear reduction** then makes the rollers turn three times slower than the crankshaft.

Feed a stalk, then press **Play** or turn the crank one revolution at a time. Watch the cane get gripped at the feed nip, travel over the turnplate and get squeezed again at the discharge nip.
caption: An isometric three-roller cane mill driven by a horizontal steam engine. The piston and crosshead turn a disc crank. A 20-tooth pinion drives a 60-tooth main gear on the top roller, and its 31-tooth crown gear drives equal gears on the feed and discharge rollers. Those two rollers turn the same way as each other and opposite to the top roller. Feed a stalk, turn the engine and use the optional section view to watch round cane flatten into a ribbon at two nips. Idealized kinematics only.
